summary: A roundup of 2023 fall and early winter high school sports highlights, pairing standout athlete performances in soccer, football, cross-country, diving, basketball, wrestling and swimming with quotes from their coaches. The second half covers the coaches' philosophies on character building, training tactics and the bond with athletes. The piece argues coaches shape both athletes and future citizens.
one_line: Profiles of standout high school athletes from September to December 2023, with coaches discussing mentorship, training and character development.
key_facts: The 2023 school year sports season began on September 1st.
On September 10th, Jefferson High's soccer team drew 2-2 with Lincoln Academy, with striker Miguel Torres scoring both goals.
On October 15th, Washington High School running back Malik Jones set a school record with four touchdowns in a single game.
Junior Hannah Smith of the Panthers Cross Country team broke the school's long-standing 5k record at the October 23rd invitational meet.
Springfield High diver Carlos Ramirez overcame an ankle injury to take first place in the November 4th diving competition.
On November 17th, Roosevelt High's girls' basketball team beat Madison Prep when point guard Lisa Johnson hit a three-pointer in the final seconds.
Central High School captain Jacob Lee won all his matches at the December 5th tri-meet and was named 'Most Valuable Wrestler'.
At the December 12th Winter Invitational, Eastside High swimmer Elena Rodriguez set personal bests in the 100m freestyle and 200m individual medley.
Coach Robert Ellis (football) says the aim is to instill discipline, teamwork and resilience, and that the true victory is seeing athletes grow into leaders.
Coach Tony Patel (wrestling) stresses drilling fundamentals, saying athletes must be sound in basics before complex moves.
Coach Diane Summers (cross-country) focuses on mental toughness, using visualization and strategic rest.
Coach Michael Phelps (diving) and Coach Mark Spitz (swimming) are noted as having no relation to the Olympians of the same names.
Coach Laura Hernandez (soccer) and Coach Phelps both highlight the lasting bond and trust between coaches and athletes.
